Perhaps you need some <color=batting_pitch_yellow>new members</color>?
I overheard some conversation about baseball at <color=batting_pitch_yellow>New Gaudi</color>, you know!

<color=batting_pitch_yellow>Color Commentator Miyaken's Advice</color>

Your team is kinda hurting out there...
Why don't you use a <color=batting_pitch_yellow>Training Ticket</color> to whip those guys into shape?

<color=batting_pitch_yellow>Color Commentator Miyaken's Advice</color>

You're really giving up runs out there!
You've gotta <color=batting_pitch_yellow>switch out pitchers when their stamina runs out</color>.

<color=batting_pitch_yellow>Color Commentator Miyaken's Advice</color>

Seems like you're still kind of feeling your team out. Are you
having trouble getting <color=batting_pitch_yellow>on base</color>? Your <color=batting_pitch_yellow>team's strength</color>
will go up if you get a hit during critical moments in the game.

<color=batting_pitch_yellow>Color Commentator Miyaken's Advice</color>

Your batters are going downhill here. Have you tried changing the lineup?
 Switching the lineup based on the player's <color=batting_pitch_yellow>condition</color> is one way to do it.

Choose a player to train using a <color=batting_pitch_red>Training Ticket</color>.
*Limit one Training Ticket per player per game.

A well-rounded player who not only specializes in outfield roles,
but can also fill in for all other positions except pitcher.
He's got a great RBI average, and he's a heavy hitter to boot.
As the glue of the team, he's the key to victory.

A fast outfielder who's always making contact with the ball.
Speed is his pride, allowing him to cover a wide range of
positions. His flaw is that sometimes he buckles under
pressure. In hopes of overcoming his weakness, he tries to
train more mentally than physically.

A strong starting pitcher with good control. The curveball is
his secret weapon, a throw he learned from his father as a
child. When the going gets rough, though, he does tend
to get too careful. He hopes to gain more experience and
the courage to stay cool under pressure.

This catcher is also a real slugger, swinging for the fences
with every swing. His hits go flying further than anyone else
on the team, but his lack of control often leads to strikes.
He also tends to neglect training his catcher role because
batting is so much cooler.

An outfielder with a good eye for the ball, giving him a high
on-base percentage. He handles fielding and base running
flawlessly as well, making him a near perfect player.

A first baseman with a nice batting average. He was an honor
student with a talent for just about everything of course,
and when the bases are loaded, it's his time to shine - he'll
aim to bring those runners home and all the glory with it.

Aside from his main position at third base, he excels at
playing shortstop. People tend to think of him as a fielder,
but his batting average is nothing to scoff at. A utility player
who can clean up at the top or create opportunities at the
bottom, you can count on him to get it done.

Although he prefers second base, he's a utility infielder who
can fill in any role just fine. He tends to get swept up in the
moment, though. This is great if his team is doing well, but
he'll suffer if the team is flagging.

A fast infielder who also excels at making contact with the
ball. Once he gets on base, he applies immense pressure to
the opposing team with his sheer speed. But knowing how
fast he is has led to an obsession with running speed, and his
teammates often need to bully him into focusing on his
fielding and batting.

A slugger with a batting average he can take pride in. His
immense concentration at the plate, even when pinch
hitting, is second to none. Problem is, hitting is all he
cares about, so his fielding and base running averages are
pretty subpar.

A reliable catcher who brings out the best in his pitchers.
He's a great communicator, and understanding the team's
chemistry and quirks makes him ideal for support. He's
not bad at the plate, either.

The whole team counts on this slugger to step to the plate and
get results, and he often does just that. He's a decent fielder
as well. His downside is drinking too much at post-game parties.

An outfielder who prides himself on both his power and
accuracy. For whatever reason, he's especially reliable at
tipping the game in his favor at the bottom of the 9th.
Although his fielding isn't as great as his batting, he does
have some nice utility in both infield and outfield roles.

A lead-off hitter who loves a challenge. Don't expect any
distance from him, but if you just need a guy to get on base,
his excellent control and speed make him your man. He's
the life of the party too, keeping his team's spirits high when
they're losing with rowdy shouting and friendly smacks.

If he connects with the ball, you can expect a home run from
this herculean hitter. People often compare the speed of his
swing to a ceiling fan set on kill. He loves practicing his batting,
but that's literally the only thing he'll practice.

An outfielder with good speed and strong defense. He's a
fielding enthusiast who traps fly balls like a vice. He's also a
pretty accurate hitter, but not an especially powerful one.

An aloof batter who strives to reach baseball zen in his pursuit
of the perfect swing. His dedication to this leads to friction
with his team, but at the end of the day, they acknowledge
that he's a great batter. He's also a skilled fielder and runner.

This skilled infielder likes to show off how great he is, which
sometimes leads to errors. He's also got a powerful swing, but
he tends to make intimidating poses when he gets on base that
can lead to friction with the opposing team.

A southpaw equipped with a dangerously fast and accurate
fastball. He's practically a strikeout factory when he busts
out his forkballs, but his stamina wears down fast, so it's best
to pull him before he starts giving up runs.

A relief specialist who's got some mean breaking balls.
It's like he was born to be a relief pitcher, excelling at
late-game entries and crumbling whenever he starts.

A player with the perfect pitching skill set who can even stay
cool and collected under pressure. Maybe his lack of flaws
is a flaw, in its own way.

An ace rookie with a wealth of hidden talents. Although he
really devotes himself to practice, he's too young to have
experienced true failure, so he starts to buckle if he lets a
few hits go. He'll be one to watch<symbol=em_dash_with_outline>will he rise to greatness,
or remain saddled by his insecurities?

<color=batting_pitch_yellow>Batting</color> and <color=batting_pitch_yellow>Slugging</color> <color=batting_pitch_red>increase moderately</color>.

<color=batting_pitch_yellow>Batting</color> and <color=batting_pitch_yellow>Slugging</color> <color=batting_pitch_red>increase greatly</color>.
<color=batting_pitch_yellow>The success rate of base stealing</color> <color=batting_pitch_red>increases moderately</color>.
